test_title: PYST 10: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which economic system dominated India on the eve of independence (in 1947)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Colonial agrarian economy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's economy during the time of independence in **1947** was primarily an agrarian economy. This means that agriculture was the dominant sector, employing around **85% of the population**.
 
• The British colonial rulers had established an exploitative economic system that focused on **extracting resources** from India and exporting raw materials to Britain.
 
• The British introduced the **zamindari system** (land revenue system), which led to the exploitation of farmers. Farmers were heavily taxed, and many were left in poverty.
 
• The colonial economy was structured in a way that hindered industrial development in India. Instead, it promoted the imports of British manufactured goods, creating an imbalance in trade.
 
• The economy lacked significant industrialization, with limited development in sectors like textiles, steel, and other manufacturing industries. As a result, India depended heavily on agriculture.
 
• The infrastructure, such as railways and communication systems, introduced by the British was largely meant to serve their own administrative and economic interests, such as the transportation of raw materials.
 
• By the time of independence, India had a **low per capita income**, high levels of poverty, and widespread unemployment, which were the result of prolonged colonial exploitation. *Hence, the correct answer is "Colonial agrarian economy."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Colonial Agrarian Economy:**

 
 
• The economy was predominantly rural, with the majority of people engaged in **subsistence agriculture.**
 
• India became a supplier of raw materials like **cotton, jute, and spices** to British industries and a market for their finished goods.
 
• There was a lack of modern agricultural technology, leading to **low productivity** and frequent famines.
 
• The **zamindari system** and other land revenue systems caused widespread exploitation of farmers by landlords and moneylenders.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Colonial Rule on India’s Economy:**
 
 
• The Indian economy faced **deindustrialization**, particularly in the traditional handicrafts and textile industries.
 
• The **drain of wealth** theory, as explained by **Dadabhai Naoroji**, highlighted how resources were extracted from India to enrich Britain.
 
• The lack of capital investment in industries and infrastructure for the benefit of Indians left the country economically backward.
 
 
 
• **Contrasting Economic Systems:**
 
 
• **Import substitution industrialization:** Adopted later in India post-independence to reduce dependency on imports and promote domestic industries.
 
• **Global free market:** India did not adopt this system at the time of independence, as the focus was on self-reliance and economic recovery.
 
• **Socialist planned economy:** This system was introduced in India after independence with the adoption of the **Five-Year Plans** starting in 1951.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The British policies resulted in **stagnant economic growth**, with the agricultural sector unable to sustain the growing population.
 
• The **per capita income** during the colonial period barely increased, and the standard of living of the average Indian deteriorated.
 
• The colonial economy left India with a legacy of poverty, high illiteracy rates, and underdeveloped industries, which the country had to address post-independence.
